newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke - Labour's spending plans don't add up.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke - Labour's spending plans don't add up.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke on Friday accused the opposition Labour Party of meeting questions about financing its policies with "deafening silence".
"Labour's sums just don't add up," Clarke told a Conservative Association meeting at Nottingham University. "They have spending commitments they cannot fund."

The Chancellor said Labour had not come clean on how they would fund their spending commitments, including stating which companies would be liable for the "windfall" tax on privatised utilities and how much they expected to raise.

Clarke questioned how Labour could keep the current Conservative government's spending plans for the next two years, when these plans included future privatisations and savings on reform of the social benefit system -- policies to which he said Labour were opposed.

"Whilst pretending to accept our income tax rates and our spending plans for two years, they refuse to explain how they would raise the money missing through several key Tory policies...which they do not plan to follow if elected to power," Clarke said.
"Labour's hollow tax and spend prospectus is a terrible indictment of their unfitness to govern."
An election must be held in Britain by May 22 at the latest.
